sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau, 2023 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, individual unit file
Colorado Secretary of State TRACER: contributions to Elbert County candidates since 2023
EFF Atlas of Surveillance (police surveillance technology, searched by department)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
The county borrowed $1,260,000 during the year, which is not counted as revenue but helps explain spending above revenue.
Debt service leaves out $1,169,000 of principal repaid with new borrowing the county did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Payments to other governments ($453,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts itemized cash contributions from businesses, unions and political committees to Elbert County candidates whose committee names a county office, reported to the Secretary of State's TRACER since 2023. Committees whose names do not show the office are left out, so this is a floor. Individuals, LLC members, in-kind gifts and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Colorado yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Third-party investigative platform
redFlags.detail: The Elbert County Sheriff’s Office received an enterprise license for LexisNexis' Accurint Virtual Crime Center through its membership in the Colorado Information Sharing Consortium.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012741, citing Government information

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Elbert County Sheriff's Office operates one drone as of 2017, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003242, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College

redFlags.label: Flock camera network

Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
